passages.text: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul came to the brothers in Corinth.
Paul did not use eloquent words.
Paul did not use human wisdom.
Paul proclaimed the testimony about God.
passages.original: Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί ἦλθον οὐ καθ’ ὑπεροχὴν λόγου ἢ σοφίας καταγγέλλων ὑμῖν τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul visited the believers in Corinth.
Paul made a decision while he was with them.
Paul chose not to focus on any other knowledge.
Paul decided to know only one thing among them.
Paul chose to know Jesus Christ.
Paul chose to know Jesus Christ as the one who was crucified.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔκρινά τι εἰδέναι ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον

passages.text: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul came to the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul came in weakness.
\r\nPaul came in fear.
\r\nPaul came with much trembling.
passages.original: κἀγὼ ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἐν τρόμῳ πολλῷ ἐγενόμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power, so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul spoke to the Corinthians.
Paul gave them a message.
Paul preached to them.
Paul did not use persuasive words of human wisdom.
Paul showed the power of the Holy Spirit.
Paul showed the power of God.
Paul did this so their faith would not depend on human wisdom.
Paul wanted their faith to depend on God's power.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ λόγος μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμά μου οὐκ ἐν πειθοῖς σοφίας λόγοις ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀποδείξει Πνεύματος καὶ δυνάμεως ἵνα ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν μὴ ᾖ ἐν σοφίᾳ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλ’ ἐν δυνάμει Θεοῦ

passages.text: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom—but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.
passages.sermon:
We speak wisdom among the mature.
This wisdom does not come from this age.
This wisdom does not come from the rulers of this age.
The rulers of this age are coming to nothing.
passages.original: Σοφίαν δὲ λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖς τελείοις σοφίαν δὲ οὐ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου οὐδὲ τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου τῶν καταργουμένων

passages.text: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.
passages.sermon:
We speak about God's wisdom.
This wisdom is mysterious.
This wisdom is hidden.
God chose this wisdom long ago.
God chose it before time began.
God chose it for our glory.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ λαλοῦμεν Θεοῦ σοφίαν ἐν μυστηρίῳ τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην ἣν προώρισεν ὁ Θεὸς πρὸ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς δόξαν ἡμῶν

passages.text: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
passages.sermon: The rulers of this age did not understand God's wisdom.\r\nThey did not know it.\r\nIf the rulers had understood God's wisdom, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
passages.original: ἣν οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἔγνωκεν εἰ γὰρ ἔγνωσαν οὐκ ἂν τὸν Κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταύρωσαν

passages.text: Rather, as it is written: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”
passages.sermon:
God has prepared great things for those who love Him.
No person has seen these things with their eyes.
No person has heard these things with their ears.
No person has imagined these things in their heart.
Scripture says this.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται Ἃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἀνέβη ὅσα ἡτοίμασεν ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
passages.sermon:
God has revealed this to us.
God used the Spirit to reveal it.
The Spirit searches everything.
The Spirit searches even the deep things of God.
passages.original: Ἡμῖν γὰρ ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ Θεὸς διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος Τὸ γὰρ Πνεῦμα πάντα ἐραυνᾷ καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.
passages.sermon:
A person has a spirit inside him.
This spirit belongs to the person.
Only this spirit knows the person’s thoughts.
No other person knows these thoughts.
God has a Spirit.
Only the Spirit of God knows God’s thoughts.
No one else knows the thoughts of God.
passages.original: τίς γὰρ οἶδεν ἀνθρώπων τὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ οὕτως καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐδεὶς ἔγνωκεν εἰ μὴ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.
passages.sermon:
We are Christians.
We did not receive the spirit of the world.
We received the Spirit who comes from God.
God gave us His Spirit.
God gave us His Spirit so we can understand His gifts to us.
God freely gave us these gifts.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα εἰδῶμεν τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ χαρισθέντα ἡμῖν

passages.text: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.
passages.sermon:
We speak about these things.
We do not use words taught by human wisdom.
We use words taught by the Spirit of God.
We express spiritual truths with spiritual words.
The Spirit teaches us how to speak about spiritual things.
passages.original: ἃ καὶ λαλοῦμεν οὐκ ἐν διδακτοῖς ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας λόγοις ἀλλ’ ἐν διδακτοῖς Πνεύματος πνευματικοῖς πνευματικὰ συνκρίνοντες

passages.text: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.
passages.sermon:
The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God.
He thinks these things are foolish.
He cannot understand them.
These things must be understood in a spiritual way.
passages.original: Ψυχικὸς δὲ ἄνθρωπος οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Θεοῦ μωρία γὰρ αὐτῷ ἐστίν καὶ οὐ δύναται γνῶναι ὅτι πνευματικῶς ἀνακρίνεται

passages.text: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.
passages.sermon:
The spiritual man judges all things.
No one can judge the spiritual man.
The spiritual man has understanding from the Spirit of God.
He can discern what is true and right.
Others cannot judge or fully understand him.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς ἀνακρίνει τὰ πάντα αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπ’ οὐδενὸς ἀνακρίνεται

passages.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
passages.sermon: No one knows the mind of the Lord.\r\nNo one can instruct the Lord.\r\nWe have the mind of Christ.
passages.original: Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν Κυρίου ὃς συμβιβάσει αὐτόν ἡμεῖς δὲ νοῦν Χριστοῦ ἔχομεν
